pinterest.title: Interactive Wedding Seating Chart Ideas Where Guests Take, Find or Do Something
pinterest.description: An interactive wedding seating chart turns the walk to your table into a small moment of its own. Guests take a card tied to a sweet or a named glass of champagne, find their name on a wall of photos or an illustrated map, or scan a code on arrival. Finish the table plan first, then choose the display. Ideas for an intimate dinner or a large reception, with the practical checks that decide whether each one holds up on the night.

pinterest.title: A Sweet Touch, a Glass of Champagne and a Pop of Colour: Interactive Seating Chart Ideas
pinterest.description: Wedding seating chart ideas guests walk away holding. Tie each name and table to a wrapped macaron or sugared almonds, set out named flutes of champagne as a welcome drink (with something without alcohol alongside), tuck escort cards into sprigs of rosemary, hang tagged brass keys on a board, or greet guests at a tropical reception with chilled coconuts. Keep edible and floral pieces out of the sun until the last moment.

pinterest.title: How to Make an Interactive Wedding Seating Chart Easy for Every Guest to Read
pinterest.description: Treat your seating display as a sign before it is decor. Use generous type, keep names and table numbers in the same place on every card, and check it at the hour guests arrive. Alphabetical by surname is quicker to search on a long list. Place it where guests arrive, away from doorways and the bar, viewable at every height, with a clear path in front. Keep a printed list nearby so the display is never the only way to find a seat.

slides: An interactive wedding seating chart turns the walk to your table into a small moment of its own. Here is how to choose one.
First, finish the table plan. Every interactive display is only as reliable as the list behind it.
Take something: a card tied to a sweet, a named glass of champagne, a favour in a strong colour, tagged keys on a board.
Find something: a wall of photos or cards, an illustrated map with tables named after places that matter to you, names written on an antique mirror.
Do something: a screen or a code to scan on arrival. Keep a printed list and a person who knows the plan nearby, too.
Make it easy to read: generous type, names in the same place on every card, a sensible height and a clear path in front.
Marrying overseas? Ask the venue where the display can stand, how early it can be set up, the rules for wind and rain, and whether there is power at the entrance.
Planning a wedding abroad? Message us to talk it through with a Wedded Advisor. Link in bio.
instagram_carousel.caption:
A standard seating chart is read. An interactive one is used. Each guest picks up a card, lifts a drink, scans a code or searches a wall of photographs, and in doing so learns their table.

Our refreshed guide groups the ideas by what guests do at the display:
- Take something: a wrapped macaron or sugared almonds tied to a name card, a named flute of champagne as a welcome drink, chilled coconuts at a tropical reception, tagged brass keys on a board.
- Find something: a seating wall, an illustrated map with each table named after a place in your story, names written by hand on a mirror.
- Do something: a screen or a code on a printed sign, which handles a large guest list well and is the easiest style to change at the last minute.

Whatever you choose, a few checks decide whether it holds up on the night:
- Finish the table plan first, then choose the display.
- Alphabetical by surname is quicker for guests to search on a long list.
- Make it viewable at every height, with a clear path in front, and keep a printed list nearby.
- Outdoors, weight or clip every card and agree a covered backup spot.
- Print a few blank cards in the same style, and give one person, not either of you, the master list on the day.

Build the plan itself in Wonderland Studio, our planning app for seating charts and RSVPs, so the list you send to the stationer is the same list your RSVPs produced.

Planning a wedding abroad? Message us to talk it through with a Wedded Advisor. Full guide at the link in bio.
